title: backpressure-aware-queue-manager-and-priority-smoothing-for-continuous-batching
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: In high-concurrency production traffic we observed occasional starvation of medium-latency requests by very high-parallel KV-heavy tails. This PR introduces a backpressure-aware queue manager and a priority-smoothing policy that reduces starvation risk while preserving batching efficiency. Summary of changes: 1) Introduced a per-queue token regulator that tracks effective inflight weight using a fast-exponentially-weighted moving average (EWMA) of active tokens; queues that exceed a configurable soft-budget accrue backpressure and are temporarily deprioritized for new batch assembly. 2) Added an age-based smoothing factor so items that waited beyond an age threshold get boosted into the next batch (prevents indefinite postponement). 3) Implemented an in-flight KV pin hint: when a request includes heavy KV usage we mark the KV pages as "pinned_hint" for the batch window so subsequent small requests are preferentially scheduled onto different workers (reduces head-of-line blocking). 4) Adaptive tail timeout extension: head-of-line requests that are close to finishing their kv-cache priming can request a micro-extension (configurable up to 30ms) to avoid aborting batches and regressing throughput. 5) Telemetry: new metrics for queue_backpressure_score, queue_age_boosts, kv_pin_conflicts and micro_timeout_extensions to make tuning observable.
Design notes: - The backpressure regulator is lightweight and lock-free in the hot path: it uses per-core counters with periodic aggregation to avoid contention. - Priority smoothing uses a compact two-bin aging counter (fast and slow age buckets) to keep memory overhead low. - The KV pin hint is advisory only; actual KV memory pinning remains managed by the cache; the hint simply influences scheduling to avoid co-locating heavy KV loads.
Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for regulator math and aging boost rules - [x] Integration test in benchmark-lab with mixed KV-heavy and KV-light workloads - [x] CI perf benchmark before/after (95th/99th/mean) - [x] Docs: scheduler tuning guide updated with new knobs - [x] Observability: dashboards and alert rules added
Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind runtime.scheduler.v2 and enabled in Canary pool for 72h before account-wide rollout. Observability thresholds set to detect increased p95 or reduction in throughput and to automatically rollback.
Impact: In internal Canary runs with a 70/30 mix (kv-heavy/kv-light) we saw 8% median latency improvement for kv-light requests, 14% improvement in 99th percentile completion time for mixed workloads, and no measurable loss in aggregate token throughput. Related: ENG-4821 (kv-tail incident post-mortem), ENG-4890 (scheduler tuning spike).

+ pub struct BackpressureRegulator { // EWMA of tokens per-queue

+ }

+ // Age boosting: if wait_ms > AGE_THRESHOLD && boost_count < MAX_BOOST -> promote
+ if wait_ms > AGE_THRESHOLD { boost_request(req); }

+ // KV pin hint attached to req metadata; advisory only
+ req.metadata.insert("kv_pin_hint", KvPinHint::Suggested);
review_thread: Comment (Miguel): Can we avoid adding a global lock when aggregating per-core counters? Author reply: aggregation is done on a timer and uses atomic add/cas; no global mutex. Comment (Lena): The micro-extension sounds risky for latency SLOs. Author reply: ext is bounded and only applied when the request is already primed; we rolled it out to Canary and observed fewer aborts. Request (Ravi): Add an e2e test that mixes 1k concurrent small requests with 100 long KV requests. Author: added integration in benchmarks and documented results.
ci_summary: All CI jobs passed: unit, integration, lint, and performance bench. One flaky test in bench harness was quarantined and fixed in a follow-up commit.
release_notes: Added backpressure-aware queue manager and priority smoothing to reduce starvation of medium-latency requests in mixed KV workloads. New tuning knobs: runtime.scheduler.v2.backpressure_alpha, runtime.scheduler.v2.age_threshold_ms, runtime.scheduler.v2.micro_timeout_ms. Metrics added: scheduler.queue_backpressure_score, scheduler.queue_age_boosts, kv.kv_pin_conflicts.
notes_for_ops: Feature is feature-flagged. Recommended Canary config: enable for one Canary pool, set backpressure_alpha=0.15, age_threshold_ms=12, micro_timeout_ms=20. Watch scheduler.queue_backpressure_score and kv.kv_pin_conflicts for unexpected spikes.
testing_notes: Bench harness scenario: mixed_kv_workload.json (70% kv-heavy, 30% kv-light), run 10 minutes with steady-state ramp and collect p50/p95/p99 and throughput. Compare against baseline. Integration tests added to benchmark-lab job id: bench-20260221-07.
